title: U.S. House · Pennsylvania's 11th Congressional District
area: South-central Pennsylvania: Lancaster County and part of York County.

context.text: Lloyd Smucker was unopposed in the May 19, 2026 Republican primary. Nancy Mannion defeated Sarah Klimm in the Democratic primary. Jeffrey Wilder (Independent) did not make the general-election ballot, according to Ballotpedia.

candidates.name: Lloyd Smucker
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative (since 2017); member, House Committee on Ways and Means and House Committee on the Budget

summary.text: Lloyd Smucker is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 11th District, first elected in 2016. He previously served as a Pennsylvania state senator (2009-2016) and on the West Lampeter Township board of supervisors. For the 2025-2026 Congress he serves on the Joint Economic Committee, the House Committee on Ways and Means, and the House Committee on the Budget.

background.text: Attended Franklin and Marshall and Lebanon Valley Colleges.
Served as a Pennsylvania state senator from 2009 to 2016, and previously served on the West Lampeter Township board of supervisors (2005-2009) and planning commission (2001-2005).
Owned his own construction company from 1981 to 2005 before entering elected office.

priorities.text: Statement on the Working Families Tax Cuts says the Congressional Budget Office confirms the cuts are "accelerating the growth of the American economy."
priorities.quote: When it comes to economic growth, the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) has one thing right—the Working Families Tax Cuts (WFTC) are accelerating the growth of the American economy.

priorities.text: Introduced legislation to renew and expand the Work Opportunity Tax Credit, intended to help connect disadvantaged individuals to jobs.

positions.summary: Supports the Working Families Tax Cuts and describes them as accelerating economic growth, rather than raising taxes on high earners or corporations.
positions.quote: the Working Families Tax Cuts (WFTC) are accelerating the growth of the American economy

positions.summary: Voted for H.R. 2, the Secure the Border Act, and has visited the U.S.-Mexico border multiple times, criticizing what he called the Biden administration's border policies.
positions.quote: Rep. Smucker (PA-11) voted in favor of H.R. 2, the Secure the Border Act.

record.text: Assigned to the Joint Economic Committee, the Committee on Ways and Means (Social Security, Tax, and Trade subcommittees), and the House Committee on Budget for the 2025-2026 Congress.

Introduced the Improve and Enhance the Work Opportunity Tax Credit (WOTC) Act, updated in November 2025, to strengthen and extend a tax credit intended to help disadvantaged individuals secure employment.
Voted for H.R. 2, the Secure the Border Act, in May 2023.
Sponsored legislation described by his office as strengthening Social Security and protecting children from identity fraud, passed by the House with near-unanimous support in December 2025.

candidates.name: Nancy Mannion
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19 Democratic primary, defeating Sarah Klimm

summary.text: Nancy Mannion is a registered nurse and healthcare leader with decades of experience as an emergency nurse and international healthcare consultant. She is challenging incumbent Lloyd Smucker, campaigning on affordability, health care, and restoring public trust in government.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from Salem State College in 1988 and a graduate degree in nursing from the University of Maryland School of Nursing in 1995.

Spent decades working as an emergency nurse and providing humanitarian medical care in South America, Asia, and Africa; also worked as an international healthcare consultant helping bring clinical standards to Europe, Asia, and the Middle East.
Recognized as a Fellow by the American Academy of Nursing and the Emergency Nursing Association, according to her own account.

priorities.text: Says she wants to make life more affordable for district residents, citing farmers struggling with tariffs and fertilizer costs, small businesses facing regulatory burdens, and families struggling to afford groceries and health care.
priorities.quote: Real Care. Real Change. Nancy puts people first: she cares about the issues those in her district care about, whether it's a farmer struggling with tariffs and the high cost of fertilizer, or the small business owner tapped in government red tape.

priorities.text: Cites her nursing career as the basis for evidence-based, pragmatic decision-making, and says she wants to "cool down" partisan political debate.

positions.summary: Supports patients' rights to make their own health care decisions and access to affordable coverage and prescription drugs, and says the nation should prioritize public health and medical research.
positions.quote: Nancy supports patients rights to make their own healthcare decisions, access affordable courage and prescription drugs, and know our nation has prioritized public health and medical research.

positions.summary: Cites farmers struggling with tariffs and higher fertilizer costs as an example of the district's affordability problems.
positions.quote: a farmer struggling with tariffs and the high cost of fertilizer

candidates.researchNotes: No prior elected office; positions are drawn from her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response. Her campaign website could not be reached within the research budget.
